fwci: Typical work: for works published 2024–2026, the median FWCI is 0–0.62. In every year, half of the works received at most 62% of the citations expected for similar works worldwide (FWCI 1 = world average).
Above the world average: 11%–45% of the works per year have an FWCI above 1, most in 2025 (45%).
Not cited: on average 52% of these works have FWCI 0, meaning no citations within their four-year window. That is why many boxes start at 0.

Mean versus median: the mean is above the median in 3 of 3 years, because a few highly cited works pull the average up. The widest gap is 2026: mean 0.38, median 0, top work 3.92. The median is the better guide to a typical work.
Still counting: works from 2024–2026 have not completed their four-year citation window, so their values will rise. Do not compare them with older years yet.
Small base: the values for 2024–2026 are based on only 10–29 works (lighter box or hollow point), so read them with care.
citations: Typical work: works published 2024–2026 have a median of 0–1 citations each; the highest median (1) is in 2024–2025.
Most cited works: the top 10% of works published in 2024 have at least 4 citations each, the highest P90 in the chart.
Not yet cited: more than half of the works published 2026 have no citations so far. This is expected for recent works and is not a sign of low quality.

Mean versus median: the mean is above the median in 3 of 3 years, because a few highly cited works pull the average up. The widest gap is 2024: mean 2.1, median 1, top work 10. The median is the better guide to a typical work.
Recent years: works from 2024–2026 have had less than three years to be cited, so their values will rise.
